title: terraform-proxmox deployment.json (desired-state INPUT)
description: Contract for the private desired-state input fetched from the on-prem S3-compatible object store at plan/apply. Its job is to REJECT an empty or structurally-broken input before any plan runs, so a missing/blank file can never produce a destroy-all plan. additionalProperties stays true so per-environment extras and `_*comment` keys never false-fail; only the load-bearing shape is enforced.

external_ingress.description: Optional SSO-gated HTTP routes to external hosts, keyed by ingress hostname label.

iso_base_url.description: Base URL of the internal read-only object prefix holding OS install media. No trailing slash: the ISO resources append their own separator, so a trailing slash yields a double slash and a 404 mid-apply.

network_domains.description: Optional VLAN name => DNS domain override, for VLANs whose UniFi network domain differs from `domain`. A VLAN absent here uses `domain`.

llm_large_serving_host.description: Short hostname of the heavy-tier LLM serving host. Optional: this host is a fixed-address reservation rather than a PVE guest, so it is absent from `containers` and cannot be derived. Published to consumers as constants.serving.host.

llm_large_serving_ip.description: Reserved address of the heavy-tier LLM serving host (bare IPv4, no mask). Optional, and omitted rather than guessed: consumers fail loudly on absence. Published to consumers as constants.serving.ip.

llm_gpu_engine.description: Single serving-engine selector for the GPU LXC set; defaults to llama_cpp when absent.

llm_cpu_scaler.description: CPU LLM pool scaler. Declare the unit name ONCE; tofu derives /opt|/etc|/var/lib paths and publishes constants.llm_cpu_scaler. Tags name which container tags select pool members. All fields optional — defaults live in modules/proxmox-stack/variables-llm-cpu-scaler.tf.

containers.description: LXC desired-state, keyed by name. At least one is required — an empty map is the empty-{} destroy footgun this schema exists to catch. `_`-prefixed keys are inline `_*comment` docs (tofu strips them) and are exempt from the entry shape.

agents.description: Optional owner roster: legacy physical agents remain keyed by container key and include name; logical owners use an owner slug key and omit name.

trust_tier.description: Memory trust tier. Legacy physical owners may omit it; logical owners must supply it explicitly.

native_binding_ref.description: Opaque reference to an existing runtime configuration. Required for logical owners; not a prompt URI or wire protocol.

workstations.description: Optional non-secret workstation identities keyed by workstation name.

host.description: DNS name used to reach the workstation.

nodes.description: Cluster node identity, keyed by node name. At least one required.

guest_naming_exceptions.description: Guest names exempted from the node-digit naming law, name -> reason (modules/proxmox-stack/checks-guest-naming.tf). Never add a name here without a reason; shrink, never grow.

node_services.description: Per-node (DaemonSet-style) service templates, keyed by service name. OpenTofu expands each into one container per node listed in per_node (locals-node-services.tf). `_`-prefixed keys are inline comment docs.

proxmox_user.description: Proxmox login user (bare OS/PAM user, no realm) for every Proxmox SSH and UI login

vdi_preserved_vlans.description: VLAN keys (into network_cidrs) whose subnets VDI guests keep reaching over the LAN rather than through a VPN client running inside the guest. Published to the Ansible inventory as vdi_preserved_cidrs. Omit or empty to disable.

nixos_ct_template_url.description: URL of the NixOS LXC template tarball built by nix-ai (nix build github:dryvist/nix-ai#herdr-lxc-template, published as a release asset). Absent or empty disables the download and, with it, any NixOS guest.

nixos_ct_template_file_name.description: vztmpl file name the NixOS template is stored as. Must match the value a guest's ct_template references.

nixos_ct_template_sha256.description: sha256 of the NixOS LXC template, so content drift is rejected at download time. 64 lowercase hex characters.

resource_profile.description: One set of resource figures; used for both expected_resources.avg and .peak.

io_read_mbps.description: Storage read throughput in megabytes per second.

io_write_mbps.description: Storage write throughput in megabytes per second.

net_in_mbps.description: Inbound network throughput in megabits per second.

net_out_mbps.description: Outbound network throughput in megabits per second.

node_input.description: A single node's identity, matching modules/proxmox-stack/variables-infrastructure.tf's `nodes` object type exactly. additionalProperties is false HERE (unlike most of this schema) precisely because of logical_id: with additionalProperties true, a misspelled or mistyped logical_id key is not a validation error, it is silently accepted as an unknown extra property, and the node it belongs to silently opts OUT of the guest node-digit naming law — every one of its guests stops being judged, with no error anywhere. Closing this object converts that failure from silent to loud. If a new node attribute is ever needed, add it here rather than reopening additionalProperties.

hardware.description: Capability-shaped label, e.g. compact-node, standard-node, storage-node.

commissioned.description: false = declared but not yet installed.

nautobot_device_name.description: This node's name in the inventory system of record, when it differs from the key.

ssh_host_key.description: Reviewed SSH host public key for this node, '<type> <base64>'.

memory_budget_mb.description: Guest memory budget in MiB: physical RAM minus an explicit host reserve.

cluster_roles.description: Cluster-wide roles this node plays, e.g. storage. Exactly one node must claim each role.

tags.description: Capability tags consumed by Ansible to derive node groups and select matching roles.

logical_id.description: The node's logical digit for the guest node-digit naming law (modules/proxmox-stack/checks-guest-naming.tf). Unset opts the node out of naming enforcement entirely — see the object description above for why that makes this the one key in this object that must never be allowed to typo silently.

node_service_template.description: One per-node service template. Only the shape the generator dereferences unconditionally is required; per_node keys MUST be keys of `nodes` — JSON Schema cannot express that cross-sibling constraint, so it is enforced by the postcondition on data.aws_s3_object.deployment in main.tf.

per_node.description: Node key -> instance allocation. `_`-prefixed keys are inline comment docs.

container_input.description: A single container's desired-state. Only the fields that break addressing/identity if absent are required; everything else is free. node_name is among them: it used to be optional and tofu silently fell back to the primary node, so omitting it was indistinguishable from choosing it.

expected_resources.description: Expected guest resource use (SHOULD; a plan warns when avg or peak is missing). Reference for capacity planning and telemetry comparison.

peak.description: Maximum observed or expected peak resource use.

hostname.description: Guest hostname. A container tagged gpu-passthrough uses an Ada Lovelace or Blackwell generation, GDDR 6 or 7 with optional uppercase X, an integer VRAM value followed by GB, and a role suffix.

tags.description: Guest tags. GPU containers carry gpu-passthrough; llm-gpu-small selects the pinned small-model role, while llm-gpu-small-router selects the extra GPU-serving endpoint and also requires gpu-passthrough. The router tag does not select llm-gpu-small. Node capability is declared separately with the nvidia-gpu node tag.

node_name.description: Proxmox node this container is placed on. Must be a key of `nodes`.

migrate.description: When true, migrate this container instead of replacing it when node_name changes. If unset, defaults to true when ha_replication_target is set and false otherwise; explicit values win.

adopt.description: Marks a live container that state tracks under another node, or not at all. imports.tf adopts it in place instead of planning a create. Unset or false is the steady state; remove the flag after the adopting apply has landed.

llm_gpu_engine_identity.description: Immutable engine identity for one member of the GPU serving LXC set.

ct_template.description: OS template override, as a bare vztmpl filename on datastore_iso. Absent = the estate's shared Debian template. A NixOS guest sets this together with os_type="unmanaged". SET-ONCE: template_file_id is in the container module's lifecycle.ignore_changes, so changing it on a live guest is a no-op.

ha.description: Enrol this guest in Proxmox HA (modules/proxmox-stack/ha.tf). Default false. Enrolling also accepts the relocation-vs-state hazard documented in imports.tf: HA moves a guest, refresh 404s it on the node recorded in state, and the failed apply freezes the published ansible_inventory. Enrol a guest whose state cannot be rebuilt from code.

ha_affinity_group.description: Negative-affinity group name. Guests sharing a value are kept on separate nodes by a proxmox_harule. Only meaningful with ha=true, and only takes effect with two or more members.

ha_replication_target.description: Node holding this guest's pvesr copy and the only node HA may relocate it to on node loss.

openbao_cluster_input.description: Parameterized OpenBao LXC cluster generator. OpenTofu expands this into regular containers so shared peer config is defined once.

placement.description: Map of Proxmox node name to OpenBao peers. An integer item is a suffix that drives name, VMID, and IP host octet. An object item names the peer by its vm_id: the host octet is vm_id minus vm_id_base, and the name is the given hostname or else <app>-<vm_id>. An object item may set migrate for a node change.

migrate.description: For each peer, an explicit value overrides container_defaults.migrate; if both are unset, defaults to true when container_defaults.ha_replication_target is set and false otherwise.
Migration value for generated peers unless a peer overrides it; when unset, peers default to true if ha_replication_target is set and false otherwise.

ha_replication_target.description: Node holding each generated peer's pvesr copy and its only HA relocation target.
